types.name: Base rent and increases
types.tierReason: Either way: fixed rent can be calculated (tier 2), but increases tied to an index like the CPI have no cap (tier 1).

types.name: Real estate taxes
types.tierReason: No cap (tier 1): tax increases come from the city, not from anything you do.

types.name: Operating costs (CAM)
types.tierReason: No cap (tier 1): your share comes from the landlord's costs of running the building.

types.name: Late fees and interest
types.massachusettsLaw: Residential deposit and late-fee rules (c. 186, § 15B) don't cover commercial leases. Verify scope.
types.tierReason: Costs money that can be calculated (tier 2): a set charge or rate on the late amount.

types.name: Security deposit
types.massachusettsLaw: Residential deposit and late-fee rules (c. 186, § 15B) don't cover commercial leases. Verify scope.
types.tierReason: Costs money, capped at the deposit amount (tier 2).

types.name: Length of lease and renewal
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if missing a renewal deadline would cost you the space, tier 3 if it's only dates and notices.

types.name: What you can use the space for
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): what you may use the space for.

types.name: Exclusive right to sell
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): a right that protects you from competing tenants.

types.name: Condition at move-in
types.tierReason: No cap (tier 1): you may have to fix problems that were there before you moved in, which you didn't cause.

types.name: Repairs and maintenance
types.massachusettsLaw: c. 186, § 19 repair duty after notice of unsafe condition; applied to a commercial lease (Bishop v. TES Realty Trust, 2011). Verify.
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if you must fix major systems such as the roof or heating with no cap, tier 2 or 3 if only minor repairs.

types.name: Changes to the space
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): you need permission before changing the space.

types.name: Selling the business or subletting
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if the landlord can refuse a transfer for any reason, tier 3 if it needs a good reason. The versions set this.

types.name: Insurance you must carry
types.tierReason: Costs money that can be calculated (tier 2): the premiums for the insurance you must carry.

types.name: Covering the landlord's losses
types.massachusettsLaw: c. 186, § 15 voids clauses making the tenant cover the landlord's own negligence; applied to commercial leases (Norfolk & Dedham v. Morrison, 2010). Get full cite, KeyCite.
types.tierReason: No cap (tier 1): you cover the landlord's losses from claims, such as a customer's injury, that come from running the business.

types.name: What counts as breaking the lease
types.massachusettsLaw: 275 Washington St. Corp. v. Hudson River Int'l (SJC 2013): remedy clause read literally. Get full cite, KeyCite.
types.tierReason: Default rule: the general default clause doesn't raise a tier by itself (tier 3). Versions that set their own default have their own tiers.

types.name: What you owe after a default
types.massachusettsLaw: 275 Washington St. Corp. v. Hudson River Int'l (SJC 2013): remedy clause read literally. Get full cite, KeyCite.
types.tierReason: Costs money that can be calculated (tier 2): the rent for the rest of the term. No cap doesn't count, since it only follows a default.

types.name: Personal guaranty
types.tierReason: Can cost your personal assets (tier 1).

types.name: Landlord can move you
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if the landlord can move you without paying, tier 2 or 3 if it pays and finishes the new space first. The versions set this.

types.name: Landlord can end the lease early
types.tierReason: Can cost you the space (tier 1).

types.name: Landlord entering your space
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): when the landlord may enter the space.

types.name: Signs
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): what signs you may put up.

types.name: Fire, damage, or government taking
types.tierReason: Can cost you the space (tier 1): after a fire or a government taking, the lease can end.

types.name: Staying after the lease ends
types.tierReason: Costs money that can be calculated (tier 2): a set rent, often higher, if you stay after the lease ends.

types.name: Move-out duties
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if you must remove all improvements with no limit, tier 2 or 3 if only named changes or normal wear. The versions set this.

types.name: Lender paperwork
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 without a non-disturbance promise, tier 3 with one, as your brief's example says. The versions set this.

types.name: How notices must be sent
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): how notices must be sent.

types.name: Legal fees
types.tierReason: Costs money (tier 2). No cap doesn't count, since the fees only come with a dispute or a default.

types.name: Giving up a jury trial
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): how a dispute would be decided.

types.name: Your right to end early
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): a right that lets you end early.

types.name: Utilities and service outages
types.tierReason: Either way: metered bills can be calculated (tier 2), but outages with no rent reduction have no cap (tier 1). The versions set this.

types.name: Right to more space or to buy
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3): a right that helps you.

types.name: Riders and changes to the lease
triggers: in the event of any conflict
types.tierReason: Either way: a rider can change any part of the lease, so its tier depends on what it changes.

types.name: Limits on what the landlord owes you
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if your losses from a landlord's broken promise could be large, tier 3 if it only limits whom you can sue.

types.name: Delays no one can control
types.tierReason: No cap (tier 1): on the GBREB form you keep paying full rent through delays no one controls, however long they last.

types.name: The real estate broker
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3). No cap doesn't count: the cost only comes if you used a broker you didn't name.

types.name: Following laws and local rules
types.tierReason: Rules and paperwork (tier 3). No cap doesn't count: the cost only comes if your use breaks a law.

types.name: Uses that raise the building's insurance
types.tierReason: Either way: tier 1 if your normal business raises the building's insurance, such as cooking, since there's no cap. Tier 3 if it doesn't.
